create.name: Great Vow Zen Monastery
create.bio:
Great Vow Zen Monastery is the residential training centre of the Zen Community of Oregon, set on forty wooded acres above the Columbia River flood plain, about eighty miles north-west of Portland near Clatskanie. Its co-abbots, the Zen teachers Jan Chozen Bays and Hogen Bays, founded it in 2002 and still lead it; Chozen has taught the community since 1985 and is known for her books on mindfulness and mindful eating, while Hogen trained with Philip Kapleau and Taizan Maezumi and later with Shodo Harada. Practice follows Maezumi's White Plum line, which joins Soto and Rinzai Zen, and draws on Tibetan and Theravada methods too.

Lay and ordained residents live a full monastic day of dawn and evening meditation, work, formal meals and chanting, with a silent week-long sesshin most months and practice periods through the year; residency is open by application. Visitors can come for weekend Beginner's Mind retreats that teach the basics of Zen meditation, and in the forest are the Jizo Garden, where people remember those who have died, and a shrine where visitors leave tokens of their aspirations. A sister temple, Heart of Wisdom, serves the community in Portland. Decades of recorded talks, a chant book and many short videos are shared freely online.

courses.title: Sesshin at Great Vow
courses.description: A week-long silent retreat, held most months, with eight to ten hours of zazen a day, work practice, formal meals, talks and interviews with a teacher. Newcomers are advised to attend a weekend introductory retreat first.

courses.title: Residential Program
courses.description: Full-time residential practice at the monastery, with several hours of daily meditation, community work, chanting services, classes and monthly sesshin, usually begun within a seasonal practice period. Applications go to the residency coordinator.

courses.title: Beginner's Mind Weekend Meditation Retreat
courses.description: A silent weekend at the monastery for people new to intensive Zen practice, opening with thorough meditation instruction and following a retreat schedule of sitting, chanting, formal meals and work. In person only.

courses.title: Monastery Winter Practice Period
courses.description: Eight weeks of residential practice in the quiet of winter, following the monastery's daily round of zazen, work, classes, retreats and formal meals. Enquiries go to the director of training.

free_resources.title: ZCO Teachings Archive
free_resources.description: A historical archive of recorded talks from sesshin and other events going back decades, with chant recordings, searchable by speaker and year. Free to listen to or download.

free_resources.title: Zen Community of Oregon Chant Book
free_resources.description: The community's book of chants and liturgy used at the monastery and its temples, free to download as a PDF.
